content.introduction: Gold miner Newmont (NEM) was the S&P 500's best performer for the week with a 24.4% gain, and it was up 47.7% for 2025. Freeport McMoRan (FCX) also made the list with a 14.4% gain for the week, although it ended with a 12.4% decline for 2025. Nine companies among the week’s 20 best-performing stocks were in the technology sector, including Nvidia (NVDA), which was up 17.6% for the week but ended with a 17.4% decline for 2025. The information-technology sector was the week's leader with a 9.7% gain, but it was still down 15.3% for 2025. Two defensive sectors - consumer staples and utilities - ended the week with year-to-date gains. Four sectors ended Friday at levels lower than they were at the end of 2021 - consumer discretionary, materials, healthcare, and real estate.
body:
Here are the 20 stocks in the U.S. large-cap benchmark index showing the largest price increases for the week through Friday:

Gold miner Newmont (NEM) was the S&P 500's best performer for the week with a 24.4% gain, and it was up 47.7% for 2025. Freeport McMoRan (FCX), which also mines gold and other metals, made the list with a 14.4% gain for the week, although it ended with a 12.4% decline for 2025. [...] The information-technology sector was the week's leader with a 9.7% gain, but it was still down 15.3% for 2025. Two defensive sectors - consumer staples and utilities - ended the week with year-to-date gains.

Four sectors ended Friday at levels lower than they were at the end of 2021 - consumer discretionary, materials, healthcare and real estate.

The week's best performers among the S&P 500 [...] Nine companies among the week's 20 best-performing stocks were in the technology sector - but most were still down for this year, including Nvidia (NVDA), which was up 17.6% for the week but ended with a 17.4% decline for 2025.

Rounding out the largest 10 components of the index, Apple (AAPL) rose 3.5% for October through, while Microsoft (MSFT) was up 1.8% for the month, Tesla (TSLA) was up 12.7% and Eli Lilly (LLY) soared 22.5%.

One more Big Tech tidbit: SpaceX (SPCX) is not yet a component of the S&P 500; it's stock declined 10.7% during October.
